questions.text: Upfront Fare Transparency: Clear pricing: (1) Upfront fare estimate (before booking); (2) Breakdown of fare (base, distance, time, surge); (3) Surge pricing notification (multiplier); (4) Toll/parking fees disclosure; (5) Cancellation fee clarity; (6) Comparison with alternatives (public transport); (7) Historical pricing visibility.
questions.evidence_required: Fare calculation algorithm, Surge pricing policy, User interface screenshots
questions.africa_specific_notes: Surge pricing often opaque. Users need to know the multiplier upfront. Comparison with matatu (minibus) helps decision-making.

questions.text: Driver Earnings Transparency: What drivers earn: (1) Commission rate disclosure; (2) Breakdown of deductions (platform fee, insurance, penalties); (3) Incentive structure clarity (bonuses); (4) Comparison of gross vs net earnings; (5) Visibility of trip-level earnings; (6) Explanation of rating impact on earnings; (7) Transparency on 'ghost trips' (unpaid cancellations).
questions.evidence_required: Driver earnings dashboard, Commission structure docs, Deduction policy
questions.africa_specific_notes: Drivers often don't understand deductions. 'Ghost trips' (accepted but cancelled by passenger) are a major complaint.

questions.text: Safety Incident Reporting & Disclosure: Transparency on safety: (1) Public safety report (aggregate incidents); (2) Response time to safety incidents; (3) Outcome disclosure (driver suspension/deactivation); (4) Transparency on insurance claims; (5) Collaboration with police (crime reports); (6) User notification of nearby incidents; (7) Safety feature effectiveness (SOS button usage).
questions.evidence_required: Safety transparency report, Incident response logs, Insurance claim stats
questions.africa_specific_notes: Platforms often hide safety incidents. Public pressure (e.g., after high-profile assault) forces transparency.

questions.text: Driver & Vehicle Information: Know before you ride: (1) Driver name and photo; (2) Vehicle make, model, color, plate number; (3) Driver rating and trip count; (4) Real-time location sharing; (5) Emergency contact visibility; (6) Vehicle inspection status; (7) Driver license verification badge.
questions.evidence_required: App interface screenshots, Verification badge logic
questions.africa_specific_notes: Passengers need to verify driver/vehicle before entering. Fake drivers (using someone else's account) are a risk.

questions.text: Location Data Usage & Sharing: Who sees your location: (1) Purpose of location tracking (trip only vs always); (2) Sharing with third parties (advertisers, government); (3) Retention period for trip history; (4) User control over location sharing; (5) Anonymization for analytics; (6) Explanation of background location access; (7) Opt-out options.
questions.evidence_required: Privacy policy, Location data policy, User consent flows
questions.africa_specific_notes: Location data can reveal home/work addresses. Risk of stalking or government surveillance. Users need control.

questions.text: Trip History & Data Portability: User access to data: (1) Can user download trip history?; (2) Can user delete trip history?; (3) Data retention policy; (4) Sharing trip data with employers (corporate accounts); (5) Access by law enforcement (transparency on requests); (6) Export format (PDF, CSV).
questions.evidence_required: Data export feature, Deletion policy, Law enforcement request transparency report
questions.africa_specific_notes: Corporate accounts often track employee movements. Law enforcement requests common (crime investigations).

questions.text: Rating & Deactivation Logic: Explain the algorithm: (1) How ratings are calculated (weighted average?); (2) Threshold for deactivation; (3) Appeal process for low ratings; (4) Impact of false accusations; (5) Explanation of 'acceptance rate' impact; (6) Transparency on 'preferred driver' logic; (7) Bias testing (discrimination).
questions.evidence_required: Rating algorithm documentation, Deactivation policy, Appeal process
questions.africa_specific_notes: Drivers fear arbitrary deactivation. Passengers sometimes give low ratings for discriminatory reasons (tribe, accent).

questions.text: Surge Pricing & Demand Prediction: How surge works: (1) Explanation of surge calculation; (2) Notification of surge before booking; (3) Historical surge patterns (predictability); (4) Cap on surge multiplier; (5) Transparency on demand prediction model; (6) Impact of events (concerts, rain) on surge.
questions.evidence_required: Surge pricing algorithm, Historical surge data, Regulatory filings
questions.africa_specific_notes: Surge during rain can be exploitative. Regulators (e.g., Kenya) have tried to cap surge. Transparency helps acceptance.

scoring_notes: Layer 2 (Transparency) for Transport in SSA: Pricing transparency (surge) and driver earnings transparency are trust-builders. Safety incident disclosure is a regulatory and public pressure issue.
